issueTitle: Gate All Pull Requests with Gilfoyle Security Architect

stories.title: Define the Gilfoyle security contract
stories.description: Define Gilfoyle's tunable prompt, security taxonomy, threat model, structured findings, evidence requirements, version attribution, and blocking policy on the shared adversarial-agent schema.
acceptanceCriteria: Gilfoyle owns a dedicated human-editable prompt file with an explicit version and content hash
Prompt, schema, policy, tools, and model versions are independent and attributable
The policy blocks high and critical findings and uncertainty about security-control bypasses while medium findings remain advisory
Findings require confidence, category, exact citations, exploit or failure scenario, impact, remediation, and verification guidance
stories.notes: Added a disabled, independently hashed Gilfoyle registration with a versioned prompt, security schema, policy, bounded-tools contract, engine identity, contract validator, tests, and developer documentation. Full yarn validate passed.

stories.title: Collect security context and trust boundaries
stories.description: Extend the shared bounded collector with security-specific trust boundaries, data flows, authentication, authorization, dependencies, workflows, Bicep, containers, configuration, contracts, and manifests.
acceptanceCriteria: Security context covers every issue-required repository surface without executing pull-request code
Trust boundaries, privileged identities, data sources, sinks, and control changes are explicit
Untrusted content cannot alter Gilfoyle's prompt, tools, policy, or workflow behavior
Missing mandatory security context produces a blocking configuration result
stories.notes: Extended the shared Git-object-only collector with an independently hashed Gilfoyle context profile covering all required repository surfaces, explicit trust boundaries, privileged identities, sources, sinks, and changed controls. Trusted agent selection and protected control-plane declarations keep pull-request instructions inert; missing, binary, truncated, or incomplete mandatory security context blocks. Focused proofs and full yarn validate passed.

stories.title: Integrate deterministic security evidence
stories.description: Feed Gilfoyle versioned evidence from deterministic security checks such as CodeQL, dependency review and audit, secret detection, workflow policy, Bicep analysis, and container scanning where applicable.
acceptanceCriteria: Deterministic security checks run independently with immutable actions and least privilege
Gilfoyle cannot override, downgrade, or mask deterministic failures
Unsupported repository surfaces are explicit rather than silently skipped
Evidence inputs remain attributable and bounded
stories.notes: Added a final fail-closed Continuous integration aggregate over independent validation and read-only deterministic security jobs. Pinned CodeQL and dependency review, dependency audit, redacted secret detection, workflow policy, pinned Bicep compilation, and explicit unsupported-container handling produce a bounded exact-head manifest that Gilfoyle must validate and cannot override. Focused checks, fail-closed simulations, and complete yarn validate passed.

stories.title: Attest protected calibration provenance
stories.description: Add non-forgeable protected-workflow calibration provenance that binds exact code, registered configuration, Azure identity, benchmark inputs, report artifacts, trusted workload identity, and verified timestamps before promotion can consume a report.
acceptanceCriteria: A cryptographically verified attestation binds the protected workflow run and attempt to the exact repository and head commit
The signed predicate binds registered agent/config fingerprints, Azure deployment and workload identity, benchmark inputs, and report and artifact digests
Unsigned, untrusted, replayed, mismatched, stale, duplicate, or tampered evidence fails closed
Deterministic policy and tests prevent repository-authored JSON from self-asserting promotion
Operators can generate and verify retained evidence without secrets or raw tokens
stories.notes: Added a GitHub Sigstore artifact-attestation contract, protected-run predicate builder, exact signer/source/run verifier, pinned repository and Azure workload policy, replay/freshness/tamper defenses, 29 focused tests, and operator documentation. The complete yarn validate suite passed. No calibration was run and Gilfoyle remains disabled and unpromoted.

stories.title: Implement, calibrate, and promote Gilfoyle
stories.description: Implement the security-architect reviewer, prompt-injection defenses, seeded vulnerable and safe benchmarks, severity calibration, false-positive evaluation, bounded cost and latency, and protected-run attested promotion.
acceptanceCriteria: Benchmarks cover authorization bypass, injection, secret exposure, workflow escalation, dependency risk, Bicep privilege, archive traversal, unsafe deserialization, race conditions, and cleanup leaks
High and critical seeded issues and control-bypass uncertainty are blocked at the promotion threshold
Safe examples and medium advisory cases remain within the approved false-positive threshold
Prompt changes invalidate and rerun Gilfoyle calibration
Model, tool, timeout, malformed-output, and service failures fail closed
Only a threshold-passing Azure report with a valid US-004A protected-run attestation can be promoted
stories.notes: Calibration implementation and the dedicated keyless Azure deployment remain live with strict thresholds unchanged. Protected main run 31575384182 executed the materially distinct tuned 24-case configuration at exact head 2bb2fc0485c0fc6b17912410fad17677be4d59f8 but failed closed: 0% blocking detection, 0% safe false positives, 0% advisory escalation, 100% evaluator errors, 100% agreement across identical errors, 13.552-second p95 latency, 11 missed critical scenarios, and 7 missed control-bypass cases. Azure telemetry observed 47 HTTP 200 model requests, 133,702 input tokens, 29,295 output tokens, and an estimated $0.100353 cost. Threshold failure prevented report upload, predicate creation, attestation, verification, and promotion. The original and tuned protected configurations have both failed real-Azure calibration, so the materially distinct final-run allowance is exhausted. US-004B is blocked; Gilfoyle remains disabled and unpromoted pending a separately authorized investigation and protected-main recalibration cycle.

stories.title: Register the Gilfoyle GitHub pipeline
stories.description: Register Gilfoyle as an isolated required check on the shared Azure runtime with fork safety, retained structured evidence, annotations, bounded concurrency, and no shared mutable state with other agents.
acceptanceCriteria: Every pull request receives one Gilfoyle check and relevant pushes rerun it
Gilfoyle cannot start until the complete deterministic continuous-integration workflow succeeds for the same head commit
Forks receive no secrets, privileged credentials, unrestricted tools, or executable workflow control
The check publishes concise annotations and a retained validated JSON artifact
Gilfoyle has an independent prompt, policy, calibration, check name, and exception scope
Shared max-three concurrency cannot let one agent suppress or impersonate another

stories.title: Add emergency exception and outage handling
stories.description: Implement auditable narrow emergency exceptions, service-outage behavior, retry boundaries, diagnostics, and administrator procedures.
acceptanceCriteria: Exceptions require authorized owner, issue, exact finding fingerprint, rationale, narrow scope, audit evidence, and expiry within 24 hours
Expired, malformed, unrelated, reused, or overly broad exceptions fail closed
Service outages, timeouts, cancellation, and invalid output remain blocking
Retries apply only to identified transient infrastructure failures and preserve original evidence
Administrator emergency actions are documented and auditable

stories.title: Deploy and enforce Gilfoyle
stories.description: Deploy and calibrate Gilfoyle end to end, prove fail-closed behavior, integrate Ralph remediation, document operations and prompt tuning, and require the promoted check on main.
acceptanceCriteria: End-to-end review, annotations, artifact, calibration, outage, and exception paths are verified
Policy tests reject missing, weakened, canceled, timed-out, malformed, bypassed, or uncalibrated Gilfoyle checks
Main branch protection requires Gilfoyle alongside existing required checks
Ralph treats Gilfoyle findings as blocking and iterates until resolved
Developers can tune the versioned prompt and reproduce findings locally
Every issue acceptance criterion is reconciled to live implementation evidence
